The Marianas are on the far eastern periphery of a disorganized,
unsettled pattern over Yap State, centered around Joint Typhoon 
Warning Center (JTWC)'s Invest 96W. 96W is currently located near 
Yap Proper around 8N139E. A weak, shallow trough extends northeast 
from 96W to the west of the Marianas, and a second weak trough 
extends eastward from the disturbance, passing to the south of Guam. 
The positioning of these features is steering moderate southeast 
winds across the islands this afternoon, with patches of scattered 
showers developing within the convergent flow east to southeast of 
Guam. Invest 96W will meander very slowly over the next day or so, 
stalling somewhere just north of Yap and maintaining a more unsettled
pattern for the Marianas through at least Wednesday night. On 
Wednesday, gentle southeast winds may become light and variable at 
times, and allow for the development of scattered island showers over
Guam in the afternoon, especially if skies clear by around mid day. 
A fairly dry pattern will set up by the end of the week, with a 
return to moderate to fresh trade winds this coming weekend.

Marine...
Light to moderate southeast winds will prevail for the next day 
or two. Winds will continue to diminish through Wednesday, 
gradually coming up to gentle to moderate for the latter half of 
the week, then increase to moderate to fresh this weekend. 
Combined seas of 4 to 6 feet will relax by another foot or so 
through tonight as the trade swell weakens, becoming 3 to 5 feet 
for the next few days. Trade winds and swell will come back up 
this weekend, and combined seas will become 5 to 7 feet once more
around Saturday. Meanwhile, there is a moderate risk of rip currents
along north and east facing reefs, and there will be a moderate risk
for lightning tonight through Wednesday night. A high risk of rip 
currents may return along east facing reefs this weekend as the trade
wind and swell reinvigorate, leading to an increase in east facing 
surf.

Tropical Systems...
A weak tropical disturbance, JTWC's Invest 96W, is centered south-
southeast of Yap Proper near 8N139E, moving slowly west-northwest. 
Invest 96W is currently rated sub-low, meaning it is not expected to 
develop into a significant tropical cyclone over the next few days. 
96W is producing moderate to deep convection across Yap State, with 
numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms now present over Yap 
Proper. Little to no development is expected with 96W as it moves 
past Yap Proper. Invest 96W will be monitored closely over the next 
few days for any signs of strengthening.

Eastern Micronesia...
Latest satellite imagery shows partly cloudy skies with isolated 
showers over all three forecast points this afternoon. An Inter-
Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is seen to the north of Majuro and
Kwajalein, with a surface trough to the south. Altimetry shows seas
of 3 to 6 feet across the region, with higher seas to the east of 
the Marshall Islands.

The main change in the forecast is in the short term, with lower 
POPs (Probability of Precipitation) across the region. The ITCZ
remains the primary weather producer for the next few days, however,
it has been a bit slower to fire up than previously expected. A
southwest to northeast oriented trough is now moving west-northwest
and looks to begin to interact with the developing ITCZ to bring
increased convection to Majuro later tonight. As the ITCZ continues
to develop, the convection is expected to spread west as the ITCZ
strengthens over Kosrae and eventually Pohnpei. The ITCZ looks to
remain active through the end of the week, then fragment over the
weekend. It does look to remain fairly active for Majuro through the
weekend. Although an overall unsettled pattern does look to continue
across the region through the weekend, Pohnpei and Kosrae are 
expected to see a decreasing trend in convection.

Marine conditions don't look to change drastically. Mostly light 
winds are expected at Kosrae through the weekend, with light to 
gentle winds at Pohnpei. Majuro can expect gentle to moderate winds 
through Saturday. Combined seas look to increase a little by the 
weekend, with Kosrae seeing seas of 4 to 6 feet by the end of the 
week. Pohnpei can expect seas as high as 7 feet over the weekend, 
while Majuro is expected to briefly hit as high as 8 feet.

Western Micronesia...
There are two main features that will bring unsettled weather to the
region. The first is a surface trough with a weak embedded 
circulation (Invest 96W) over Yap State, and the second is a trade- 
wind trough over eastern Yap State.
